name: MI-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Polymarket prices Democratic win near certain
McKinney won renomination with substantial fundraising and outside support
Republican nominee has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: The seat's D+22 lean and the Democratic nominee's clear financial edge make a Republican win implausible, and markets price the race at 98% Democratic. The open seat adds some uncertainty, so the margin sits slightly below the fundamentals-based estimate.
model.watch: Any late outside spending for the Republican nominee or an unusually strong GOP environment in Michigan could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Shri Thanedar (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Detroit-area MI-13 is a heavily Democratic open seat after Shri Thanedar lost renomination. Donavan McKinney enters the general with strong fundraising and outside backing, while Republican T.P. Nykoriak has reported little financial activity. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 98 percent, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive.

The district's D+22 partisan lean and a favorable national environment for Democrats point to a comfortable margin in the mid-20s. With no public polling available, uncertainty is somewhat elevated, but the structural fundamentals leave little realistic path for a Republican upset.
